newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rexrodt convinced Germany to meet EMU terms in 97.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt convinced Germany to meet EMU terms in 97.

text.p: German economics minister Guenter Rexrodt said he was convinced that Germany would meet the Maastricht convergence criteria in 1997 and that there was no doubt the single currency would be launched in January 1999.

"I am convinced that Germany will meet the convergence criteria for the 1997 test year and that it will then meet the demands of the stability and growth pact," he said in an interview with French daily Le Figaro to be published on Thursday. An advance copy was made available to Reuters.
German industry and banks need to aim for a precise date so they can prepare for change of currency, he said.
"There must be no doubt that economic and monetary union will start on January 1, 1999," he said.
He added that in addition to the short-term goal of a timely launch of the euro single currency, public finances needed to be brought under control.

"There is not only the short-term objective of a punctual launch of economic and monetary union. What will be decisive, and what needs urgently to be implemented, is the consolidation of public finances" he said.
Germany expects to raise 17 billion marks from privatisations this year, he said.
This includes 10 billion marks from the sale of a further tranche of Deutsche Telekom shares to the state development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW), which will then sell them on.
Shares in Deustche Postbank AG will raise three billion marks, he said. There are also plans to sell shares in airline Lufthansa on the stock market, as well as other state assets.
In 1998, the sale of more Telekom stock will raise 15 billion marks and stakes will be sold in airports.
Between now and 2000, the government will dispose of all its major holdings except the post and the railways, he said.
He added that he was confident that 1997 would see real growth of 2.5 percent.
"...I am confident that the 1997 year will see real growth of 2.5 percent," he said.
The German cabinet is due to meet on Friday to discuss a supplementary budget for 1997 and 1998.
